Equivalence partitioning.d: A test design technique: split all possible inputs into groups (partitions) that the system should treat the same way, then test one value from each group instead of every value.

Boundary value analysis.d: A test design technique that tests values at the edges of each valid range (just below, on, and just above the limit), because bugs cluster at boundaries.

Decision table.d: A table listing every combination of conditions and the expected action for each, used to test business rules with several inputs.

Pairwise testing.d: A combinatorial technique that covers every pair of input values at least once, using far fewer test cases than testing every combination.

Gherkin.d: A plain-language format for describing behaviour as scenarios using Given (starting state), When (action) and Then (expected result). Used in BDD tools such as Cucumber.

Traceability matrix.d: A table that links each requirement to the tests that cover it, so you can see what is tested, what isn't, and what a change affects.

Assertion.d: The check inside an automated test that decides pass or fail, for example 'the total shown should be £90'. A test without a meaningful assertion proves nothing.

Page object.d: A test-automation pattern where each page or component of an app gets one class holding its locators and actions, so tests read clearly and selectors are changed in one place.

Flaky test.d: An automated test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without any change to the code, usually because of timing, shared state or unstable test data.

Fixture.d: In a test framework, reusable setup (and clean-up) that tests ask for by name, such as a logged-in page or a fresh test user.
